# Independent audit of the all-dimensional incidence-crossing simplex family

Audited source: `candidate f8b9dc8a138f0e0c`.

**Result: PASS.** All geometry, coarea normalizations, exact selected-row
formulas, and the two-level-vector argument check without repair. The source
correctly proves only the displayed family and makes no general-simplex or
mixed-integer conclusion.

## 1. Actual simplex and all parameter branches

The edge matrix from P_0 is

    (t+C)I+(A/d-C)11^T.

Its eigenvalues are t+C with multiplicity d-1 and A+B in the remaining
direction. Thus the printed determinant is exact. Since C<0, B>0 and
A+B>0; excluding C=-t removes the only zero determinant. The branch C<-t
is still a legitimate full-dimensional simplex, with the possible change
of determinant sign handled by ordinary absolute volume. No additional
orientation assumption is needed.

The printed barycentric coefficients are positive, sum to one, and give
zero because sum_(j>=1) P_j=B1. Hence zero is interior. The balanced normals
have exactly the stated signed vertex values. In particular all cuts are
proper, with no boundary vertex for C<0, and the last d caps each contain d
strict vertices.

## 2. Cap and section factors

Row zero isolates P_0 with positive margin A and equal negative margins
-B, giving Q_0=(A/(A+B))^d and S_0=dQ_0/A.

For every other row, its complement isolates P_0 with positive margin A/d.
The d edge denominators are one copy of A/d+t=1/d and d-1 copies of
A/d-C=D/d. Hence the complementary fraction is exactly A^d/D^(d-1),
and its normalized coarea is d/(A/d) times that fraction, which is the
printed S=d^2 A^(d-1)/D^(d-1). The original and complementary caps share
their section, so this S is also the required section for the original
large cap. Boundary volume is zero.

The normalization then telescopes:

    Q_0/S_0=A/d,
    dQ/S=(D^(d-1)-A^d)/(d A^(d-1)),

whose sum is D^(d-1)/(d A^(d-1)). Substitution yields exactly the two f-levels
in (4). No per-row normal rescaling has entered these calculations.

## 3. Selected row and strictness

Using d(A+B)=1+(d-1)A-d(d-1)C, subtracting the complementary-cap term
from f_0 gives exactly

    Phi_0=d-1+A^(d-1)[1-d(d-1)C]/(A-dC)^(d-1).

With u=-dC/A>0, the final fraction becomes
(1+(d-1)Au)/(1+u)^(d-1). Bernoulli's inequality and 0<A<1 show it is
strictly less than one, including d=2 where Bernoulli itself is equality.
The limit C increasing to zero is equality in the selected row, as stated.

## 4. Two-level-vector lemma

For p=d/(d-1), the largest other row at fixed x occurs at the allowed
maximum z=d-(d-1)x^p. At that maximum, the derivative of

    F(x)=x+(d-1)[1+(d-1)(x-x^p)/d]^p

is exactly 1-U^(1/(d-1))[dr-(d-1)], where r=x^(1/(d-1)).
If dr<=d-1 it is positive. Otherwise w=1-r lies in [0,1/d), and

    U(1-dw)^(d-1)
       <=(1+(d-1)w/d)(1-dw)<=1.

The last inequality follows by expanding its product; the linear
coefficient is (d-1)/d-d<0 and the quadratic coefficient is negative.
For w>0 it is strict. Therefore F increases strictly below x=1 and
F(1)=d. This proves the lemma and the strict remaining rows in the actual
family. The d=2 exponent and x=0 endpoints cause no exceptional case.

This audit uses no unproved universal Lorentz extension. It validates an
actual non-isolated-incidence family with all its stated parameter values.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
